infoIntroP: Username Generator is a naming tool for email addresses, usernames, and other identifiers that need to be in English. It instantly creates a fresh, random name by combining two adjectives and a noun (the combination pattern is adjustable) — useful when you're stuck picking a name for a new email address, a game handle, a project codename, or any account that needs a unique identifier. It draws from a curated bank of hundreds of adjectives and nouns and uses your browser's cryptographically secure random number generator (crypto.getRandomValues), so every combination is genuinely unpredictable rather than following an obvious pattern. Regardless of your display language, the result is always generated in English so it works as a real email or username.
infoHowtoP: Click "Generate new" to get a random combination right away. Use the separator dropdown to join the words with a dot, underscore, hyphen, or nothing at all, and pick a letter case style (lowercase, camelCase, or PascalCase) to match the platform you're signing up for. Turn on "Add number" if you want a random number suffix — handy since plain word combinations are often already taken. Once you like the result, click "Copy" to copy it to your clipboard.

deepDiveP: Usernames are often hard to change once an account is created, so it's worth choosing carefully from the start. Avoid anything that could identify you personally, like your birthdate, real name, or phone number, and keep in mind that character limits vary by platform (e.g. X/Twitter caps usernames at 15 characters) — a short, generic combination works best if you want to reuse it across multiple services.

faq.a: Each result combines two different adjectives and one noun, drawn randomly from a curated word bank of several hundred entries each.

faq.q: Is the result sent to a server?
faq.a: No. Every combination is generated entirely in your browser using the Web Crypto API — nothing is sent to or stored on a server.

faq.q: Can I get a username without numbers?
faq.a: Yes. Turn off the "Add number" checkbox and the result will only contain the three words, joined with whatever separator you chose.

faq.q: I set the page to another language. Will the result be in that language too?
faq.a: No. Since this tool is meant for naming email addresses and usernames, the result is always generated in English regardless of your display language.

faq.q: Why use crypto.getRandomValues instead of Math.random?
faq.a: Math.random() is a predictable pseudo-random generator, not intended for cases where genuine unpredictability matters. crypto.getRandomValues() is the same cryptographically secure random source browsers use for security-sensitive operations, so combinations don't follow a guessable pattern.

faq.q: Could the generated username already be taken?
faq.a: Yes — this tool only suggests random combinations and doesn't check real-world availability. Check directly on the platform you plan to use.

faq.q: Should I include my real name or birthday?
faq.a: You can, but it's not recommended due to privacy risk — especially for public accounts, avoid anything that could identify you personally.
This tool generates usernames from English word combinations, since most platforms require Latin-alphabet usernames.
